title: 20.6 Fully Integrated Self-Propelling Microrobot in 180nm CMOS with Sub-GHz Parity-Time-Symmetry On-Chip Energy Harvesting and Traveling Wave Electroosmosis Actuation
problem: Autonomous motion integration remains challenging on CMOS dies—prior designs integrate energy harvesting and control, but either rely on lossy magnetic resonance coupling or require specialized photovoltaic fabrication processes incompatible with standard CMOS.
motivation: Millimeter-scale and micrometer-scale microrobots require fully autonomous integrated circuits without external power or control signals, enabling applications in medical devices and micro-scale manipulation.
method: The design harvests energy from electromagnetic waves using parity-time-symmetry (a balanced configuration that prevents energy loss) operating at sub-GHz frequencies. This harvested energy directly powers traveling-wave electroosmosis actuators—electrodes arranged in channels that create rippling electric fields, pushing fluid to generate motion. Everything is built on a single standard 180nm CMOS chip, eliminating inefficiencies from magnetic coupling or the need for specialized fabrication processes.
key_novelty: This is the first microrobot powered by combining sub-GHz parity-time-symmetry energy harvesting and electroosmotic propulsion all on a single standard 180nm CMOS chip.
contributions: Parity-time-symmetry (PT-symmetric) energy harvesting circuit operating at sub-GHz frequencies in standard CMOS
Integrated traveling-wave electroosmosis actuator with no moving parts
Monolithic design achieving full autonomy without external power or control dependencies
Demonstration of sustained motion on CMOS microbot platform
limitations: Abstract does not specify achievable speed, force output, or operating duration metrics.
primary_theme: Self-contained microrobot with integrated energy harvesting and electroosmotic actuation
